Let $N\ge0$, $I=\{1,\ldots,N\}$, source positions $z_j\in\mathbb C$ and charges $q_j\in\mathbb C$ for $j\in I$, and target positions equal to the same labelled positions. A root square is a closed square of side $s_0>0$ containing every source position. Its cells are the dyadic subsquares obtained by repeatedly bisecting each side. At each split use half-open child squares, with the outer top and right edges included in the last child, so every point belongs to exactly one child. A **finite quadtree** is a finite rooted tree of such cells in which each internal cell has its four geometric children and each leaf contains at most $s$ labels for a fixed integer $s\ge1$. Empty children are retained as geometric cells but are skipped in source and target lists. For a cell $C$, write $c_C$ for its center, $s_C$ for its side length, $I_C=\{j:z_j\in C\}$, and $a_C=s_C/\sqrt2$ for the radius of its circumscribed disk.

A cell pair $(C,D)$ is **source-separated from target-separated** when $R_{CD}:=|c_D-c_C|>a_C+a_D$; $C$ is the source cell and $D$ the target cell. For every such pair fix an analytic logarithm $L_{CD}$ on the open disk $\{w:|w-(c_D-c_C)|<R_{CD}\}$. This disk excludes zero and contains all differences $z_i-z_j$ with $i\in I_D$, $j\in I_C$. For each direct near particle pair $(j,i)$ fix one value $L_{ji}$ of the logarithm of $z_i-z_j$, when this difference is nonzero. The exact potential convention is the sum of these fixed branch values over its ordered source-target pairs; the complex derivative is independent of the chosen logarithm values.

The **recursive interaction decomposition** of an ordered pair of nonempty cells $(C,D)$ is defined as follows. If $C=D$ is a leaf, record as direct near pairs all $(j,i)\in I_C\times I_D$ with $j\ne i$. If $C=D$ is internal, replace $(C,D)$ by all ordered pairs $(E,F)$ of its nonempty children. If $C\ne D$ and $R_{CD}>a_C+a_D$, record the far cell pair $(C,D)$. If both cells are leaves and the pair is not separated, record all direct near particle pairs $(j,i)\in I_C\times I_D$ with $j\ne i$. In every other case, split a nonleaf cell of larger side length; if the side lengths tie, split the source cell. Replace the pair by the child pairs having nonempty source and target sets. Start at the root pair. The resulting lists are the **far interaction list** $\mathcal F$ and the **direct near-pair list** $\mathcal N$. Their termination and exact pair-partition property are mathematical assertions, proved separately.

For a far pair $(C,D)$ put $\rho_{CD}=(a_C+a_D)/R_{CD}<1$ and $Q_C=\sum_{j\in I_C}|q_j|$. Two leaves are adjacent when their closed squares meet. A tree is **2:1 level-restricted** when any adjacent leaves have depths differing by at most one. It is **linear-size level-restricted for this decomposition** when it is 2:1 level-restricted and there are fixed constants $C_T,C_V$ such that its number $T$ of nonempty cells and the number $V$ of recursive cell-pair inspections satisfy $T\le C_T\max(1,N)$ and $V\le C_V\max(1,N)$. A list is **bounded** when there are fixed constants $C_F,C_N$ with $|\mathcal F|\le C_F T$ and $|\mathcal N|\le C_N\max(1,N)$. The work theorem uses these explicit counts; 2:1 balance alone is not asserted to supply them.

Every nonterminal call split by [F1] has at least one nonleaf cell; each child call lowers the height of every split cell by one and leaves the other height fixed. The measure is a nonnegative integer, so every branch terminates. The recursion is finitely branching (at most sixteen child pairs at a simultaneous equal-cell split), hence its finite-depth recursion tree is finite.

If the source cell is split, its child label sets are disjoint and cover the source labels, so the child Cartesian products are a disjoint cover of $I_C\times I_D$. The same statement holds when the target cell is split. When $C=D$ is internal, splitting both ordered coordinates gives all ordered child products, also disjoint. Let $\mathbb S^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|=1\}$ with its usual surface-area measure $dS$, normalized so $\int_{\mathbb S^2}dS=4\pi$. For an integer $\ell\ge0$, let $\mathcal H_\ell$ be the complex vector space of restrictions to $\mathbb S^2$ of homogeneous degree-$\ell$ polynomials $P(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ satisfying $\Delta P=0$. Give $\mathcal H_\ell$ the inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb S^2}f\overline g\,dS$, linear in the first argument. An orthonormal basis is not fixed by this definition; the addition-theorem item proves that $\dim\mathcal H_\ell=2\ell+1$ and that such a finite basis exists.

If $Y_{\ell m}\in\mathcal H_\ell$ is later chosen from an orthonormal basis and $v\ne0$, its associated homogeneous harmonic polynomial is $H_{\ell m}(v)=|v|^\ell Y_{\ell m}(v/|v|)$. At $v=0$ use the polynomial value: $H_{00}(0)=Y_{00}$ and $H_{\ell m}(0)=0$ for $\ell>0$. This is the regular-solid-harmonic convention used in the 3D evaluator.

Restriction of a homogeneous polynomial to $\mathbb S^2$ is injective, because homogeneity recovers its value at every nonzero $x$ from its value at $x/|x|$. For each direct near particle pair $(j,i)$ fix one value $L_{ji}$ of the logarithm of $z_i-z_j$, when this difference is nonzero. The **recursive interaction decomposition** of an ordered pair of nonempty cells $(C,D)$ is defined as follows. If both cells are leaves and the pair is not separated, record all direct near particle pairs $(j,i)\in I_C\times I_D$ with $j\ne i$.
